lensFocus.spec: This run implements docs/plans/2026-11-05-db-compaction.md, only the tasks in this invocation's range (slice 1 = Tasks 1-4); retention, idempotency expiry, history GC, compaction and docs (Tasks 5-9) are out of scope, so do not flag their absence. Read the plan's Decisions 1-3 (they precede Global Constraints). Check: events.payload_format inline|delivery_ref_v1 with typed msg_id/snapshot_id columns whose CHECKs agree with the stored JSON; event_message_snapshots STRICT with UNIQUE(msg_id, body_sha256); reference record = msg_id, optional snapshot_id, base Message SHA-256, exact wire_prefix/wire_suffix, optional attachments_json, expected full Delivery SHA-256; EncodeDelivery(ctx, tx, msgID, wire) (StoredPayload, error) and HydrateBatch(ctx, q, rows) ([][]byte, error) take the caller's handle; Log.Read, ClaimDue (inside its claim tx) and notifyOperatorDeliveries all hydrate and every raw events.data reader in Task 1's inventory is covered; MCP inbox strips tokens after hydration; event_outbox.body unchanged; reference writes default off with the dual reader always on; backfill is bounded (100 rows / 1 MiB / 50 ms), resumable from a captured high-water in meta, byte-proven per row, never rewrites a hash, records ids-only exceptions and pauses on low disk/WAL pressure or SQLITE_FULL; migrations are additive next-free files with no row rewrite or VACUUM. No preference code exists in this slice.
lensFocus.security: No storage discriminator, internal reference field or snapshot id escapes to HTTP, SSE, MCP, Events callbacks, webhooks or operator notifications. Frozen blob URLs and thread summaries cannot change on retry, so recipient-scoped blob tokens are never re-minted or re-scoped at read time; MCP token stripping still applies after hydration (TestInboxCarriesNoBlobToken distinction). Bodies, Delivery bytes, URLs and tokens never appear in logs, errors, audit, backfill diagnostics or status; diagnostics are ids/counts/bytes/reason codes. SQL uses placeholders only, including the <=200-key IN batches. Hydration never reads current peers, directory, reactions, public URL or thread titles. The status path is operator-only. CLI binary stays SQLite- and eventpayload-free.
lensFocus.tests: Task 1 guards assert raw bytes or hashes per surface (never JSON-semantic equality), passed on the inline baseline and are never regenerated afterwards; Task 3 replays every guard in both storage modes. Tests use t.TempDir databases, the FakeClock, synthetic identities and no sleeps as synchronisation. Pinned: <=200 keys per query and bounded byte cache, input order preserved, no four-connection-pool deadlock when hydrating inside an open writer tx, deferred read snapshot does not take the writer lock (real modernc driver), missing/corrupt body returns no partial page, send rollback leaves no dangling refs, retries resend identical body/hash, backfill crash before/after commit resumes at the committed checkpoint, captured high-water bounds work under concurrent sends, forced SQLITE_FULL and low-headroom pauses roll back, unconvertible legacy rows stay inline with durable exception ids. Migration tests find the db migrations by name suffix, not number. Review Focus 1, 2 and 5 are each pinned by a test that fails without the behaviour.

tasks.title: Additive schema and exact-byte hydration module (`internal/eventpayload`)
tasks.refs: Plan Decisions 1, 2 (hydration seam), 3 (additive migration staging); Task 2 Interfaces; Review Focus 1, 2, 5; Global Constraints (migrations, query handles); PROTOCOL §1.3, §2.3
hazards: Files: new internal/eventpayload/{payload.go,payload_test.go} (more files inside that package are fine), ONE next-free migration `<NNNN>_event_payload_refs.sql`, migration tests (prefer a new internal/store/*_test.go file; touch internal/store/migrate_sequence_test.go or store_test.go only where an existing list must gain the file), and internal/store/store.go only for a proven deferred read-snapshot/query-handle facility. No writer cutover: internal/eventlog/log.go, internal/hub/{send.go,deliveries.go,notify.go} stay untouched (Task 3). Commit the migration/store edits separately from the eventpayload commit.

Schema exactly per Decisions 1 on the STRICT events table: `payload_format TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'inline'` with CHECK(payload_format IN ('inline','delivery_ref_v1')); nullable typed reference columns for msg_id and snapshot_id whose CHECKs force agreement with the format (msg_id non-null only for delivery_ref_v1), plus partial indexes WHERE ... IS NOT NULL for dependency queries; STRICT `event_message_snapshots(snapshot_id PRIMARY KEY, msg_id, body_sha256, body TEXT CHECK(json_valid(body)), UNIQUE(msg_id, body_sha256))`. SQLite ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN cannot carry UNIQUE/PRIMARY KEY: express identity rules as CHECKs and indexes. The ids-only backfill exception table (keyed by seq, with reason) may go in this migration; if so Task 4 adds no migration. Old migration checksums must still verify.

Interfaces: exported `StoredPayload`; `EncodeDelivery(ctx, tx, msgID string, wire []byte) (StoredPayload, error)`; `HydrateBatch(ctx, q, rows []StoredPayload) ([][]byte, error)`, where tx/q are the CALLER's query handle interfaces (a *sql.Tx or equivalent), never the pool. StoredPayload never crosses HTTP/MCP; eventlog keeps exposing envelope.Event only.

Reference record fields per Decisions 1: msg_id, optional snapshot_id, SHA-256 of the exact base Message bytes, wire_prefix and wire_suffix (exact Delivery bytes before/after the top-level `message` value, stored as JSON strings), optional attachments_json (exact send-time top-level Message attachments array, only when it differs from the canonical Message), and the expected SHA-256 of the complete Delivery bytes. Never reconstruct prefix/suffix from mutable delivery/thread/peer rows.

Use a JSON-aware top-level value scanner (escapes, nested objects, duplicate keys) to locate the `message` value and, within it, the `attachments` value; compose by byte splicing. Never regex/string replacement, never unmarshal+remarshal. Duplicate critical keys, unknown shapes or unprovable reconstruction return a typed not-convertible result so the event stays inline; never drop unknown legacy fields.

Snapshots only when the embedded Message, after removing the frozen attachment override, is not byte-equal to messages.body (or the canonical message is missing but a valid embedded Message exists); dedupe on (msg_id, body_sha256) and verify full bytes on a hash match.

HydrateBatch: at most 200 bound keys per IN query; 1 event query plus ceil(unique bodies/200) body queries, snapshot queries only when needed, never per recipient; preserve input order; batch-local cache bounded by total body bytes (8 MiB), process larger pages in chunks; no process-wide cache. Close every row iterator before nested lookups: the pool has four connections, so test hydration called inside an open writer transaction and under concurrent readers without deadlock.

Read snapshots use a deferred/read-only transaction distinct from store.Tx's BEGIN IMMEDIATE; test the real modernc driver's locking with a concurrent writer (the reader takes no writer lock and sees a consistent snapshot during a concurrent delete).
Missing or corrupt bodies return an internal storage error with no partial page; error text carries ids and hashes only, never bytes.

The immutable messages.body update guard must not break existing behaviour before cutover: make it inactive until reference writes are enabled (e.g. a trigger conditioned on a meta flag the Task 3 switch sets) and test both states. Record the chosen mechanism. Inline stays the default; no production path writes delivery_ref_v1 in this task.

tasks.title: Resumable bounded online backfill with disk-pressure stops
tasks.refs: Plan Decisions 3 (stages 1-7), 1 (snapshots, exceptions), 6 (WAL and disk headroom); Task 4 Interfaces; Review Focus 5; PROTOCOL §1.3, §12
hazards: Files: new internal/hub/storage_backfill.go and storage_backfill_test.go; internal/hub/tickers.go (slow-ticker slice hook only), hub config, cmd/vecnet-hub/{main.go,main_test.go} (additive flags: backfill enable, slice limits, and Task 3's reference-write switch if not yet exposed), an operator-only ids/counts status path, and an exception-table migration `<NNNN>_backfill_exceptions.sql` ONLY if Task 2 did not create it (next free number). No UI, MCP or CLI command in this task.

Interface: `BackfillDeliverySlice(ctx, limits)` returns progress, counts and a paused reason; cancellation safe; dry-run reports counts, ids and byte totals only. Backfill enablement is separate from reference writes and from retention, and defaults off. Default limits 100 events, 1 MiB source JSON, 50 ms target writer time; a single larger allowed event may take its own slice.

Capture the events high-water mark once and persist it with the last processed seq in the existing meta table; scan `seq > last_seq AND seq <= captured_high`, inline delivery rows only; a restart reuses them so work stays bounded; exception rows are rescanned only by an explicit rescan.

Per row: hydrate(candidate) must equal the original bytes exactly AND match any existing deliveries.body_sha256. A pre-existing hash mismatch becomes a durable ids-only exception (seq, reason) for manual review; never rewrite a hash. Snapshot insert, event update (predicate also checks the original payload_format and data) and checkpoint commit in ONE transaction; transient errors roll back the whole slice; no failed row hides behind an unrecorded checkpoint.

Disk and WAL gate through injected filesystem-capacity and checkpoint probes: available bytes must exceed max(64 MiB, 4 x slice byte limit) + current WAL bytes, else pause. Catch SQLITE_FULL, roll back, report paused and require capacity relief; never run VACUUM or an automatic shrink.

Slices run from the existing ticker with the injected clock and yield between slices through it; no long startup rewrite, no real sleeps as synchronisation. Startup recovery still resets dispatching before any maintenance starts.
The status path is operator-only and returns ids/counts/bytes/paused reason; if it needs internal/opapi/types.go or internal/httpapi/admin.go, keep the edit additive and keep the CLI SQLite-free.

Step 4's disposable backfill under concurrent sends/reads is a test on the build box in t.TempDir(), never against a live or dev hub; record worst slice duration and required headroom in the step file. Logs carry seqs, counts and bytes only.

hazards: LATER SLICE: requires prefs Tasks 1/2/4 and the prefs runtime core merged on your base (internal/prefs and *hub.Preferences with LoadSnapshot/Subscribe). If they are absent, return status blocked; never stub or copy them. Adapter acceptance completes jointly with prefs Task 3.

Files: next-free `<NNNN>_event_retention_floors.sql` with `event_retention(owner PRIMARY KEY, purged_through_seq NOT NULL, updated_at)` (initial floors 0), internal/eventlog/{log.go,retention.go,tests}, internal/hub/{ack.go,tickers.go,config}, internal/httpapi/events.go, internal/mcpserver/{resources.go,events.go}, internal/events/{store.go,worker.go} and focused tests. This task owns those mcpserver files; never connectors/**.

Consume exactly: `snapshot, err := preferences.LoadSnapshot(ctx, tx)` then `snapshot.Get("retention.ack_events")` -> prefs.Effective{Value, Source, Origin, Revision}; `preferences.Subscribe(ctx)` wakeups only refresh status/policy. On a read or validation error skip expiry and report it; never fall back to a shorter retention. No preference writer, no prefs.Get/Set/RetentionSnapshot, no second store, table or migration for preferences.

Add `OldestFor(ctx, owners)` and transaction helpers; the merged principal floor is max(purged_through_seq) over current owners; `after == floor` is valid, `after < floor` returns HTTP 409 cursor_purged with details.oldest_cursor (unchanged shape). Audit every Oldest caller, including MCP tailStart, subscribe validation/replay and pruneDone; global Oldest stays only for diagnostics.

A peer's effective pull ack is the max valid current-epoch seq of acks(P,'*'), acks(principal,'*') and acks(principal,P); never read_at, receipts, MCP scan cursors or last_seen. Live verified MCP subscriptions also need their cursor past the candidate or an exact durable outbox record.

Delete only a contiguous eligible prefix per owner, stopping at the first too-young, unacked or pinned event, and advance the floor in the same transaction. Pins: queued/pushed/held wake_idle/dispatching>0 deliveries, in-flight operator notifications, outbox pending/parked/retryable-exhausted rows; terminal suppression tombstones survive until the owning peer's floor passes the event. Bounded slices with a fresh policy snapshot inside each destructive transaction.

Archive mode suppresses hard unacked expiry while acknowledged pruning continues. Cursor strings, event ordering, epoch/AUTOINCREMENT seq and the MCP truncated response shape stay unchanged. Add lag/pin/oldest-age metrics.

tasks.title: Bounded idempotency expiry and per-send write guards
tasks.refs: Plan Decisions 5; Task 6 Interfaces; Review Focus 8; PROTOCOL §2.2, §12
hazards: Files: internal/hub/{send.go,tickers.go,send_test.go}, hub config, next-free `<NNNN>_idempotency_created_at_index.sql` (index on idempotency(created_at)), internal/audit/*_test.go and focused thread/group tests. Integrate after Tasks 4 and 5 for shared files (tickers.go order 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 7).

One effective idempotency policy shared by lookup and cleanup: default 24 h, configurable extension (48 h or more), 0 keeps keys forever, any value below 24 h is rejected. Cleanup uses the exact `< cutoff` boundary lookup uses, is bounded and indexed, returns count and cutoff, and is serialized with sends in BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions.
Response bytes and request hash are unchanged within the window; replay/conflict behaviour unchanged; reuse after expiry works.

Audit guard: send/ack/source/admin audit rows carry ids, counts and ingress only; a synthetic content/secret sentinel never appears. Do not change the audit package's production code; audit stays append-only forever.

Keep the single thread UPDATE in the send transaction; no deferred budget/activity, no count(messages) substitute. Drop no index; record a keep verdict for every index on the merged schema, including parallel additions.

tasks.title: Opt-in message-history retention with a durable thread sequence high-water
tasks.refs: Plan Decisions 4 (archive mode, confirmed exit, pins, mark/sweep, locator tombstones); Task 7 Interfaces; Review Focus 4, 6, 7; PROTOCOL §2.8, §2.9, §7, §11; hub-preferences plan Decisions 3
hazards: LATER SLICE: requires the prefs confirmation/activation adapter (hub_preference_activations with effective_from, not_before, cutoff_at, high_water) merged on your base; otherwise return blocked. Blob dependencies consume only merged blob_refs (and R2 blob_object_refs if R2 has merged); never implement R2 work.

Files: next-free `<NNNN>_thread_seq_history_tombstones.sql`, internal/hub/{send.go,reactions.go,history.go,threads.go,tickers.go}, new internal/hub/history_gc.go, opview/history readers, internal/events/store.go, blob dependency/GC tests, config and flags.

Per-thread `last_allocated_seq`, initialised from the max existing Message seq and never decreased; ordinary, reaction and participant-join paths all allocate from it BEFORE any delete is enabled. message_count, budget_remaining and last_message_at never move backwards; from_join access is unchanged.

Compact locator tombstones (msg_id, thr_id, seq, expired_at) keep `after=<purged msg_id>` pagination working with the current response shape; a direct reply to an erased Message returns the existing not-found behaviour. Report tombstone growth.

Read retention.history and retention.archive_mode from one snapshot per run and again inside each destructive slice; archive mode overrides marking, age-based hiding and sweeping, including marks made before it was enabled. Retrospective trim waits for the persisted not_before at the next nightly sweep; no PATCH, confirm or wakeup deletes anything.

Sweep order per Decisions 4; unsupported dependency classes stay pinned with a reported reason; no broad cascades; recheck pins inside each delete transaction. Audit is never deleted; blob_refs go last, then the existing blob GC decides hosted-byte deletion.

tasks.title: SQLite compaction controls, bench-hub comparison and storage release gate
tasks.refs: Plan Decisions 6, 7; Task 8 Interfaces; Review Focus 5, 8; docs/BUILDBOX.md
hazards: Files: internal/store/{store.go,store_test.go}, a new bounded maintenance helper and tests, hub diagnostics/config, integration with bench-hub's ACTUAL merged files (discover them; bench-hub merged to master in ec7a125), and a benchmark receipt under docs/business/ or bench-hub's canonical output location. Never invent a benchmark command.

Measurements (Step 3-5) run on x-boss with `BB_HOST=x-boss BB_JOBS=2 just bb GOMAXPROCS=2 ...` so they are comparable with bench-hub's x-boss baseline; this overrides the x-alpha runner for measurement commands only. Tests and gates still use the runner. Never the Fly volume, a live DB or a dev hub.

New empty databases: page_size=4096 and auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL set BEFORE tables are created and verified after init; existing NONE databases keep their mode and page size; per-connection wal_autocheckpoint in the DSN; synchronous FULL retained. incremental_vacuum at most 128 pages per slice and only where INCREMENTAL is active. Never a full VACUUM and no NONE->INCREMENTAL conversion.

Acceptance numbers are measured physical results, never the plan's logical forecasts; report F=1 even if zero. Drop no index without populated modernc EXPLAIN plus latency evidence on the merged schema.
